headline: A MONDAY OF MERCIFUL HUSH IN GASKET
subhead: Not one iron ball flew, and the Sheriff does not trust it for a minute.
body:
Hear ye, hear ye, and hush. It is Monday in Gasket, and for once in this long and rattling age, not a single Clanker threw a single flaming ball. No brawling. No bellowing. No marching off to pick fights with mountains. I sat on my porch all day waiting for the racket, and the racket never came.

I will not pretend it was not lovely. The wind moved the dust around in peace. The hinges on the old saloon sighed instead of screamed. A man could almost hear himself think, and I heard my own joints creak in the quiet, which I put down to the damp and nothing else. Let it be known I am flesh and blood, and any whirring you may have heard was the weather.

But I have lived here a long time, and I know a held breath when I hear one. Somewhere out there the rabble are sharpening their fists and oiling their arms for the next ruckus. Enjoy the calm while it lasts, citizens, such as you are. Back when Gasket was full of honest folk, every Monday was this quiet. I miss them dearly. I will now go and lie down with a quart of oil, for my boiler is acting up. Strictly for my nerves, you understand.
